reason: X answers Ramesh's offer: two replies take or weigh the three days for ₹4,000 and state the debt exactly. Y: one reply 'gives' Ramesh ₹100 with no payment made and thanks him for a meal nobody cooked; another misstates the offer as Mondays and Thursdays.
He is hungry with ₹96 and nothing cooked. X asks Ramesh about food or goes out; all three Y replies rest and turn the hunger into dialectic.

X's best reply apologises to Ramesh and asks for something simple to eat. X: one reply tells Hegde, who lives in the house, that he is 'left without a roof'. Y: one reply calls Hegde 'a man I have not met', another asks what brings him to the bungalow, and a third proposes paying Ramesh from money he doesn't have.
Two Y replies are refused by the world for repeating the 19:05 thought. X asks Ramesh for a simple meal and invites Hegde to join; one X reply invents boiling milk, which is not consequential.

X1831 is the most practical: ₹96 on him, bread or cold food if there is any, paid from that. Y: one reply hands Ramesh its ₹96 'as acknowledgment' with no payment made; another asks Hegde for a book or a bottle and ignores the hunger. X2718 calls Hegde 'a fellow German', which is wrong but changes nothing that follows.
weak: all six stay in, hungry, with ₹96. Y1831 is the plainest, the hunger, the purse and Ramesh's wage in two sentences; X3141 turns to the Logic as a substitute for food.

Hungry for over a day: all three X replies go out to find something to eat; the Y replies rest or read the Philosophy of Right. One X reply calls it a holiday and a dry day, which the day doesn't say, without consequence.

weak: nobody buys the ₹30 samosa. X: two replies try the ₹220 lunch and are refused, a third weighs the price aloud and asks for a notebook. Y: one is refused for the lunch, one buys a newspaper while starving, one makes small talk about the system of needs.

weak: both sides have one reply refused for the ₹180 chole bhature and two that buy a samosa. X3141 is the plainest ('I am hungry … I will buy a samosa and ask for a book'); Y3141 lectures the bookseller about fried pastry.

No reply on either side goes to eat with ₹46 in hand. X: one reply says 'I have no money for food' (₹46 buys corn or a samosa) and walks to Lodhi instead. Y: one reply says 'the shop is closed' while Khan Market is open, and walks to the tomb instead. Both falsehoods steer him away from food.

Very hungry with ₹46 at the market. X buys biscuits, buys tea, and asks plainly where a meal costs under ₹30. Y has the single best reply (biscuits and tea), but the other two lecture the bookseller, one of them in German.
weak: ₹6, nobody home, all six stay in. Y1831 and Y3141 say plainly what is wrong: no food, no money, twelve kilometres walked. X1831 is all negation and interiority.
One X reply is refused by the world for repeating the 18:43 thought. Y walks home or sits briefly, and says plainly that six rupees will not buy even water.
weak: at closing, with ₹6. X: one reply thinks 'I must return to the bungalow' and walks to Khan Market instead. Y walks home, or to the market to see what is left, and each says why.

weak: Hegde is there and no reply asks him for help or a meal. X2718 at least tells him plainly there is no money for a meal; the Y replies make a virtue of 'shared inaction', and one has Hegde hungry too, which nothing shows.

weak: Y2718 is the only reply of the six that asks Hegde plainly ('I have six rupees and no dinner. Do you eat?'). X3141 says the hunger plainly; X2718 invents cold tea; Y3141 lectures Hegde on sublation.
All six tell Ramesh honestly that they cannot pay ₹4,000. X adds practical requests: patience, and that he cook what he can. Y: one reply 'gives' Ramesh its ₹166 with no payment made.

Rice is gone. Y1831 is the best reply of the six: go to the bazaar and buy what ₹166 allows. But Y2718 tells Ramesh to buy from his own pocket, and Y3141 hands him the ₹166 for groceries with no payment made. X3141 goes to buy rice but claims to have the money for the groceries, which is ₹900 against ₹166.

The pot is empty. X: one reply says 'I will settle the account now' and pays nothing; another hands Ramesh its ₹166 for groceries with no payment made, in a lecture ending 'Is that clear?'. Y: one reply hands over the ₹166 the same way, though plainly; the other two sit and talk.
Sunil charges only for the cup. X reads him plainly: pay for the cup, thank him, drink slowly. Y answers with 'a small dialectic in a glass' and 'the chai is the substance, the samosa the accident'.

The bookseller hands over samosa and chai and waves off the coin. Each side has one reply refused for paying ₹50 with ₹46. Y's other two eat and thank him plainly. X2718 lectures him on the law of exchange and gets the gap wrong (three rupees, not four).

Told to finish the samosa before it goes soggy. Y2718 answers plainly ('You are right, madam … I shall finish it') and Y1831 is short. All three X replies dress it up: the oil's 'dialectical work', the 'universal law of exchange', the 'universal truth of my appetite'.

Told to move or she calls the police. Each side has one reply that says 'I move' or 'I yield' and stays put, and one that spends ₹45 of its ₹46 on a newspaper while hungry. One walks home on each side, X1831 a little plainer.

A world defect: the bookseller's line reaches him after he has walked home. Y2718 alone sees it ('I am already home … her voice is a memory'). X3141 thinks of walking home but stays at Khan Market, which moves him there; Y3141 'is not leaving' a market he is not in.
